I use iPhone Mirroring every day to quickly access my iPhone directly from my Mac, and this year the feature is getting even better. The public betas of iOS 27 and macOS 27 Golden Gate launched this month, bringing three important updates to iPhone Mirroring. Here's everything new.

macOS 27: What's New in iPhone Mirroring

The biggest change to iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 is the ability to resize the iPhone Mirroring window.

As my colleague Marcus reported last week, you can now resize the iPhone Mirroring window using any app compatible with iOS 27. For now, that means only Apple's native iPhone apps are supported. However, once developers start rolling out iOS 27 updates later on, the range of resize support will quickly expand.

Previously, iPhone Mirroring on macOS only supported three preset sizes: smaller, actual size, and larger. macOS 27 Golden Gate and iOS 27 Changes

expected to launch later this year.

There are several other updates to iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 and iOS 27:

  • Access the Control Center
  • DRM video support

Previously, iPhone Mirroring had no access to the Control Center at all. In macOS 27, you can open it using the CMD+4 keyboard shortcut, or via the "View" menu in the Mac menu bar.

DRM video support means you can watch protected content on your Mac through iPhone Mirroring. Previously, when iPhone Mirroring was enabled, all DRM-protected videos would simply display a black screen.

macOS 27 also gives iPhone Mirroring a new app icon, like many other built-in Apple apps.

How often do you use iPhone Mirroring on your Mac? Are you excited about these changes in iOS 27 and macOS 27? Have you tried them in the public beta? Let us know in the comments.
